source.title: FailSAE: Towards Interpretable Failure Prediction for Vision-Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Jie-Shu Ma; Zong-Xi Liu; Yi Zhu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares standard and failure-aware SAE training using a different measure of feature interpretability: human evaluation of whether selected SAE latent directions have class-consistent concepts. This bears on the tool-improvement part of V4, but does not measure the share of the model's own neurons that are interpretable.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates SAE latent directions, not individual model neurons or neuron poles. The reported human-evaluation percentages and label-entropy comparison bear on V4's claim that improved tools can raise interpretability. Failure-prediction performance, runtime recovery, and the analysis of concepts activated during failures do not measure the versions' claims about neuron interpretability or explanation fidelity and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on CLIP ViT-B/16 as a tool for failure prediction. Its interpretability results compare its own failure-aware SAE with a standard SAE, and the units scored are SAE latent directions, not the model's own neurons or neuron poles. No version is tested. V4 concerns the share of interpretable neurons rising with better architectures and tools. An SAE trained with a supervised failure-label loss that yields more class-specific latents is a different construct, and the class-specificity is partly built in by the objective.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that failure-aware training makes SAE latent directions more selective and class-specific, based on lower label entropy, lower activation frequency and more class-consistent concepts among top-activated directions. They also report that reconstruction error and decoder orthogonality are barely affected. Their main conclusion is that the framework outperforms baselines at failure prediction and offers concept-level explanations of failures.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains sparse autoencoders on CLIP vision-encoder representations and evaluates SAE latent directions; it does not use neuron-pole explanations or the original essay's neuron interpretability audit.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported human-evaluation shares differ between the top 5% and top 1% of directions; the comparison is between Standard and failure-aware SAE training.

fits_no_version.finding: On CLIP ViT-B/16, failure-aware SAE training raised the human-judged class-consistent share among high-activation SAE latents: 18.6% to 25.5% (top 5%) and 23.8% to 44.1% (top 1%). Mean label entropy fell from 2.598 to 1.955.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding a supervised downstream objective to SAE training increases the share of class-specific, human-interpretable SAE latents in a vision-language encoder.

record.problems: The paper does not state evaluator count, inter-rater agreement, or uncertainty for the human concept judgments. Evaluation is restricted to selected high-activation SAE directions, and the measured units are SAE latents rather than model neurons.
record.rows_left_out: Failure-prediction metrics, ablations of prediction performance, runtime recovery, and Table 4's failure-related concept counts were left out because they do not measure the interpretability-share claim in V4 or the explanation-testing claims in V6–V7. The activation-frequency distribution in Figure 3a is described as shifting toward lower frequencies, but it does not report a share of interpretable units.

record.verdict_notes: The rows were linked to V4 by the reader, but SAE latents are not neurons. The comparison is also between the study's own method and a baseline, so I reclassified the study as T4 and gave no verdicts. Human evaluation gives no rater count, agreement or uncertainty.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Compared failure-aware SAE training with standard SAE training, then human-evaluated class-consistent concepts among directions ranked in the top 5% by mean activation value.
rows.measure: Share of evaluated directions judged to have a class-consistent concept
rows.note: The paper states that the top 5% comprised 2,458 directions for the Failure-aware SAE; the Standard SAE percentage and count are also reported. The judgment concerns SAE latent directions, not model neurons.
rows.check: This measures SAE latent directions (top 5% by mean activation), not model neurons. It compares the study's own method with a standard SAE. It cannot show the neuron-interpretability share V4 names.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Compared failure-aware SAE training with standard SAE training, then human-evaluated class-consistent concepts among directions ranked in the top 1% by mean activation value.
rows.measure: Share of evaluated directions judged to represent meaningful concepts
rows.note: The paper reports these as results among the top 1% most strongly activated directions. They are SAE latent directions, not model neurons.
rows.check: Same as R1, for the top 1% of directions. These are SAE latents from the authors' own method versus a baseline SAE, not neurons.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Compared the average label entropy of latent directions for failure-aware and standard SAE training.
rows.measure: Average label entropy of SAE latent directions
rows.locator: Impact of failure-aware training on SAE; Figure 3c
rows.note: The authors interpret the lower entropy as indicating concepts more associated with specific image classes. This is a measure of SAE latent directions, not neuron poles.
rows.check: Label entropy of SAE latents is a class-selectivity measure, not a neuron interpretability share. The supervised failure-aware objective plausibly induces class-specificity directly.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CLIP ViT-B/16 SAE latent directions selected from the top 5% and top 1% by mean activation value
reader_labels.reason: Failure-aware training had higher human-evaluated concept shares than Standard SAE training in both selected groups (R1, R2); average label entropy was also lower (R3). These results support a tool/training-related increase in class-specific SAE concepts in the tested setting.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The paper's SAE-latent evaluation on CLIP ViT-B/16
reader_labels.reason: The results concern selected SAE latent directions and do not establish an interpretable share for model neurons generally, or test architecture effects or the essay's InceptionV1 estimates (R1–R3).
